compare.title: Why __PRODUCT_DISPLAY_NAME__?
compare.description: __PRODUCT_DISPLAY_NAME__ combines a TypeScript agent SDK and coding CLI. Choose a supported provider or connect a compatible local model server; setup and third-party charges depend on the provider. Public source is available under AGPL-3.0 or a commercial license.

claimSources.scope: This table compares the __PRODUCT_DISPLAY_NAME__ CLI and assembled SDK, not the bare ConversationAgent class. Features can depend on configuration, provider or host. The dated sources below cover the affected Cline claims only; other competitor entries have not been re-audited.

clineNotes.sdk: Cline provides an embeddable SDK through @cline/sdk.
clineNotes.persistence: ClineCore persists sessions and history; Cline Agent leaves persistence and lifecycle to the host, while file checkpoints are a separate mechanism.
clineNotes.background: Cline CLI supports background tasks, Zen, and schedules; these workflows do not imply the same orchestration guarantees as the __PRODUCT_DISPLAY_NAME__ CLI.

items.title: 1. Choose a supported provider
items.body: Use supported adapters for Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek and Gemini, or connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Credentials, models and charges vary by provider.

items.title: 2. Build with the SDK
items.body: Use @robota-sdk/agent-framework to assemble sessions for your own host. You supply a provider and decide how permissions, storage and lifecycle work.

items.title: 3. Inspect and license the source
items.body: The public source can be reviewed and modified under AGPL-3.0. A commercial license is available when a proprietary application cannot meet AGPL obligations.

items.title: 4. Connect a local model
items.body: Run an Ollama or LM Studio model server and configure a matching endpoint and model. Local inference still depends on your enabled tools and network configuration.

highlights.title: Public source

highlights.title: Configurable model endpoint
highlights.body: Choose a hosted provider or a local compatible server.

highlights.title: Host-owned SDK state
highlights.body: The SDK host decides whether and where to persist sessions.

highlights.title: Explicit tool permissions
highlights.body: Review permission modes and enabled integrations for the deployment.

items.q: Where do prompts and code go?
items.a: Model requests go to the endpoint you configure. A hosted provider receives the prompts and context sent to it; a local model can keep inference on your own server. Enabled web, MCP or other tools can make separate network requests.

items.q: Can we use a corporate proxy?
items.a: The model endpoint and each enabled integration must fit your network policy. Verify proxy behavior in your chosen configuration before rollout.

items.q: Can this run in a restricted network?
items.a: A local model server and internally available npm packages can support a restricted setup. Disable or configure network-capable tools according to your policy.

items.q: Is there a commercial license option?
items.a: Yes. The public source is available under AGPL-3.0, with a commercial license option for proprietary or closed-source use that cannot meet AGPL obligations. Review the licensing terms before choosing a path.
